text: Abraham had pleaded for Sodom. In Genesis 22 the three days of travel are a kind of suspended sentence, in which outwardly nothing happens, and in significance everything happens. Faith here takes the form of a structured relation or arrangement; obedience stands beside horror, and neither is suffered to prevail over the other. The instruments of the act are present before the act itself, and the narrator names them with care: the servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire.
